classification.difficultyReason: Recognise equal-side, straight-line angle and vertically opposite angle relationships in diagrams and express each algebraically without solving.

content.prompt: Write a formula describing these relationships.

spec.description: Upright unshaded square with four matching single side ticks, a right-side label and a perimeter annotation underneath.
spec.mathematics: All four sides have length a; the perimeter is P.
spec.answerVisibility: Only givens and the perimeter annotation are visible. The formula belongs to the answer.

answer.worked:
The four sides have equal length.
$$\begin{align*}P&=a+a+a+a\\P&=4a\end{align*}$$

spec.description: Diagonal straight line from lower left to upper right, with a steep upward ray from a point on the line. The acute angle is labelled a degrees and its adjacent obtuse angle b degrees.
spec.mathematics: The two labelled adjacent angles together form a straight angle.
spec.answerVisibility: The angle labels are givens. No formula or numerical angle values are supplied in the student diagram.

answer.worked:
Adjacent angles on a straight line sum to $180^{\circ}$.
$$\begin{align*}a+b&=180\end{align*}$$

spec.description: A diagonal straight line intersects a steep nearly vertical straight line. Black arcs retain the four angle sectors. The upper-right and lower-left acute sectors carry the two expressions.
spec.mathematics: The angles labelled (2z+7) degrees and (x+10) degrees are vertically opposite.
spec.answerVisibility: Both angle expressions are givens; their equality is answer-only.
